title: Grammar: comparative adjectives and as … as
competency: Use comparative adjectives and as … as to compare calendars.

keywords.def: An adjective that compares two things, with -er or more, followed by than: older than, more attractive than.
A structure that shows two things are equal: "as old as"; "not as … as" shows they are not equal.

en.text: Use a comparative adjective plus "than" to compare two things. One-syllable adjectives add -er (old → older). Adjectives ending in -e add -r (fine → finer). Consonant-vowel-consonant adjectives double the last letter (big → bigger). Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y change y to i and add -er (happy → happier). Longer adjectives use more (more attractive).

am.text: ሁለት ነገሮችን ለማነጻጸር ቅጽል + -er ወይም more + ቅጽል ከዚያም "than" እንጠቀማለን፤ old → older፣ happy → happier፣ attractive → more attractive።

screens.title: More or -er?
opts: Autumn is more attractive than winter.
Autumn is more attractiver than winter.

screens.title: Forming comparatives
paras: Use comparatives to compare two nouns or pronouns, followed by than.
In Ethiopia, June has shorter nights than other months.
In autumn, children are happier than adults.
Autumn is more attractive than winter.
After than we usually say: than me, than him, than her, than us, than them.
table: 2 syllables ending in y: y → ier

screens.title: Key words
defs: An adjective that compares two things, with -er or more, followed by than: older than, more attractive than.

screens.why: Comparatives end in -er or use more, and are followed by than.

screens.ask: "My little brother was ___ (excited) than me on Meskel day."

screens.text: "Children are ___ during the New Year holiday than on school days." (happy)

screens.ask: "The Ethiopian calendar is seven years ___ (young) than the European calendar."

opts: An elephant is bigger than a horse.
An elephant is biger than a horse.
An elephant is more big than a horse.
An elephant is bigger that a horse.
screens.ans: An elephant is bigger than a horse.

screens.text: Activity 2.20 says "The Gregorian calendar is used wider than the Ethiopian calendar." What is the better way to say it?
opts: The Gregorian calendar is used more widely than the Ethiopian calendar.
The Gregorian calendar is used wide than the Ethiopian calendar.
The Gregorian calendar is used widest than the Ethiopian calendar.
The Gregorian calendar is more wider used.
screens.ans: The Gregorian calendar is used more widely than the Ethiopian calendar.
screens.why: "Used" is a verb, so it needs an adverb: widely → more widely.
screens.clue: Which word describes how it is used?

ideas.name: as … as and the same as

en.text: Use "as + adjective + as" or "the same as" to show two things are equal: "A leap year comes as often in the Ethiopian calendar as in the Gregorian calendar." Use "not as … as" or "not the same as" to show a difference: "The Ethiopian Christmas date is not the same as the European Christmas date."

am.text: እኩልነትን ለማሳየት "as … as" ወይም "the same as"፣ ልዩነትን ለማሳየት "not as … as" ወይም "not the same as" እንጠቀማለን።

screens.title: Equal or different?
screens.ask: Both calendars have seven days in a week. Which sentence says this?
opts: The number of days in a week is the same in both calendars.
The Ethiopian week is longer than the Gregorian week.
The Gregorian week is not as long as the Ethiopian week.

screens.title: Equal and not equal
paras: Equal: as + adjective + as; the same as.
The names of the days of the week in the Ethiopian calendar are the same as in the Gregorian calendar.
Not equal: not as + adjective + as; not the same as.
The festivity dates of the Ethiopian Christmas and Easter are not the same as the European ones.
The months in the Gregorian calendar are not as many as the months in the Ethiopian calendar (12 and 13).

screens.title: Key words
defs: A structure that shows two things are equal: "as old as"; "not as … as" shows they are not equal.

opts: The Gregorian months are not as many as the Ethiopian months.
The Ethiopian months are not as many as the Gregorian months.
The Gregorian months are as many as the Ethiopian months.
The months are not as many than the Ethiopian.
screens.ans: The Gregorian months are not as many as the Ethiopian months.
screens.why: Gregorian has 12 months, Ethiopian 13; "not as … as", never "as … than".

screens.ask: "A leap year in the Ethiopian calendar comes as often ___ a leap year in the Gregorian calendar."

screens.text: Which sentence correctly uses "not the same as"?
opts: The Ethiopian New Year is not the same as the Gregorian New Year.
The Ethiopian New Year is not the same than the Gregorian New Year.
The Ethiopian New Year is not same as the Gregorian.
The Ethiopian New Year not the same as.
screens.ans: The Ethiopian New Year is not the same as the Gregorian New Year.
screens.why: "the same as" keeps "the" and uses "as", not "than". Meskerem 1 and January 1 are different days.

notes.text: Activity 2.23 b) is wrong in the book ("Ethiopian months are not as many as the Gregorian months"); the Ethiopian calendar has 13 months. The lesson uses the corrected sentence.
